[00:00] Sofia Patel: "Hey everybody, good morning, good—uh afternoon for some folks. Thanks for joining the Pulse and Pathways summit. I'll kick off with a very short state of the company, then we'll go into capacity, infra, and people.

[00:28] Rohan Malhotra (chiming in): "Quick note, sales is seeing more inbound from regulated industries asking about private deployment and on-prem options — so, there's a sense of urgency there. We'll share a list of the top 12 accounts that are asking for V-P-C.

[00:50] Sofia Patel: "Cool, that's in line with roadmap, thanks. First slide — revenue and usage. We're up 28% in host API invoiced usage quarter-on-quarter, but unit economics show some churn on long tail low-latency requests that are expensive. So the Optimize work matters.

[01:12] Liam Ortega: "On Optimize, the team's done a few experiments: smarter batching plus prefix caching gave, like, a mid-single digit token cost reduction for tiered traffic. We still need to make that recommendation easier to consume for customers — e.g., a one-click batching profile or a policy in the console.

[01:38] Nora Kim: "And to add — there was one perf regression we saw in the 70-to-90 token latency window after a kernel bump. We rolled it back; Marcus's team is running a narrow benchmark to reproduce. There's a little noise in kernel selection across GPUs that triggers in edge sequences.

[02:02] Marcus Velasquez: "Yeah, we think it's the kernel selector heuristics. We're going to add a fallback fast path and also enable a canary for the new kernel stacks. Also, on KV cache — or KV cash as the transcript had it — we saw an interesting pattern where small stateful chat sessions are getting worse P99; we want to tune the KV cache eviction thresholds.

[02:34] (brief crosstalk, someone laughs)

[02:50] Sofia Patel: "Okay, thanks. On capacity: Dedicated pockets are near 78% utilization in regions A and B. The plan is to add an extra pool and a modest burst capability, but that has cost implications — so product and finance need to align on a reprice for reserved customers.

[03:12] Rohan Malhotra: "Sales asks: can we make a clear trade-off doc for Dedicated vs Hosted (latency/cost/guarantees)? Customers want a simple matrix.

[03:27] Liam Ortega: "We will, yes. Also: private deployment pilots — a handful of customers are live in early testing. The VPC onboarding doc needs a quick polish; some networking steps are getting called out as confusing (SAML, SSO, KMS instructions).

[03:46] Nora Kim: "We saw one deployment where the customer's HSM integration caused a key rotation mismatch — ops performed a manual fix. We should add better test vectors.

[04:10] Marcus Velasquez: "And from infra, we need to improve our private control plane observability — right now audit logs are there but not surfaced. That will be a quarter one deliverable for Private customers.

[04:32] (silence, then someone says: "uh huh")

[04:45] Eve Dawson: "Shifting to people: we are pausing a few open roles to preserve runway, but prioritizing hire-in for SRE and reliability. Manager calibration will happen next week. Please be prepared for a 1:1 with your managers about hiring priorities.

[05:06] Sofia Patel: "This is a hard tradeoff; the point is we want to keep reliability work funded so we don't trade performance for growth.

[05:22] (someone murmurs agreement)

[05:30] Audience question (pulled from chat): "What is the SLA target for Dedicated after the proposed reprice?"

[05:38] Marcus Velasquez: "We're proposing a 99.9% uptime baseline with a P95 latency target; details to be finalized. The finance-team will model revenue impact if we raise performance guarantees.

[06:02] Liam Ortega: "Also note: fallback policies will become more opinionated — automatic downgrade to compatible model variants when capacity tightens. That will preserve availability but will create a product expectation we must document.

[06:26] Sofia Patel: "On the competition front — we saw a press release from Anthropic about managed endpoints; OpenAI is doing pricing simplifications, and NVIDIA keeps talking about their accelerated runtimes. It's not new, but we need to sharpen our differentiation on predictability and cost controls.

[06:50] (someone asks about partner integrations)

[07:00] Rohan Malhotra: "Partnerships are moving, we have a channel pilot with a cloud marketplace partner starting next month. That could open a few APAC regions faster.

[07:18] Nora Kim: "Small dev note — LLM kernels: we should add more deterministic benchmarking for sequence lengths; customers with long conversations (800+ tokens) see different throughput characteristics.

[07:44] (brief pause)

[07:55] Sofia Patel: "Okay, concrete wrap-up: Marcus, please draft SLA revisions and post the doc to the leadership channel by Tuesday; Liam, put together the Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoff matrix and the VPC onboarding checklist; Eve, start manager calibration. We'll have a short follow-up next Thursday to close the loop.

[08:22] (people say thanks)

[08:30] Rohan Malhotra: "One more ask from GTM: can product produce a one-pager on 'How to pick Dedicated vs Hosted' we can share with customers?

[08:40] Liam Ortega: "Yes, we'll do that and we'll include basic pricing bands, typical latency and cost ranges, and recommended use-cases.

[08:50] Audience question: "Will we continue to support legacy kernels in hosted?"

[08:56] Marcus Velasquez: "We'll maintain a compatibility window for older kernels during rollouts and offer fallbacks; it's part of the canary plan.

[09:12] (someone laughs)

[09:20] Sofia Patel: "Final note: please read the incident postmortem that Ops will publish tomorrow, comment inline, and be ready for the follow-up. Thanks again everyone.

[09:36] (closing music in recording, informal chatter)
